newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to re-open Bank Hapolaim tender.
newsitem.headline: Israel to re-open Bank Hapolaim tender.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Monday it would re-open the tender for a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim, the country's largest commercial bank.

"The government intends to sell a block of no less than 25 percent of the bank's equity now in the hands of the government and no more than its entire holding, excepting shares reserved for sale to (bank) employees," the Treasury said.

The Treasury said MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling state-owned bank shares, would publish terms of the tender early next week. It said applicants would have 45 days from then to present offers.
The announcement comes as two new groups are coalescing to bid for control of the bank. The first centres on U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil and the second around U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur Ted Arison.
Neither group has been finalised but both are believed to include partners in two earlier consortia that sought to buy the controlling stake in Hapoalim.
Claridge, an investment-holding company controlled by Charles Bronfman, has said it will take an 18 percent interest in the Arison group. It abandoned an earlier bid for the bank last August.
Israeli investor Eliezer Fishman, who had sought to lead a consortium earlier, is reportedly going to join the Keil group.

Earlier this month, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected a proposal by his economic adviser to force Hapoalim to sell its entire stakes in the Clal Israel and Koor Industries holding companies, saying such an initiative would preclude a quick sale of the bank.
